title: Post-Assessment
purpose: Measure what a new IT work-study student learned after completing assigned Launchpad modules, checklists, and shadowing.
student_intro: This is not proof that you are fully trained. Auto-scored questions show progress; written answers are saved for mentor review before readiness decisions.

readiness_levels.label: Needs More Foundation Review
readiness_levels.mentor_action: Repeat key modules and shadow closely.

readiness_levels.label: Developing Readiness
readiness_levels.mentor_action: Allow limited beginner-safe tasks with close guidance.

readiness_levels.label: Ready for Beginner-Safe Tasks
readiness_levels.mentor_action: Approve supervised beginner-safe work if local expectations are met.

readiness_levels.label: Strong Beginner Readiness
readiness_levels.mentor_action: Approve supervised work and add next-step practice.

sections.title: Confidence Reflection
sections.intro: Use 1 = Not confident and 5 = Very confident.

questions.prompt: How confident do you feel asking for help when you are stuck?
What is one thing you feel more comfortable with now than you did before training?
review_rubric: Names a concrete skill, concept, or workflow.
Shows honest reflection about confidence or remaining questions.
Gives the mentor a useful follow-up topic.
questions.mentor_use: Use this answer to guide the mentor check-in.

questions.prompt: In a workplace or school IT environment, what is a domain?

options.label: A managed environment used for accounts, computers, and access

questions.explanation: A domain helps the organization manage logins, computers, permissions, and access.

options.label: Taking a photo of a computer
Preparing a computer with the required operating system, software, settings, and configuration

questions.explanation: Imaging prepares a computer so it is ready for the correct user, department, classroom, or lab.

options.label: A record of an issue, request, task, or support interaction

questions.explanation: A ticket helps IT track work, document what happened, and know what still needs to be done.

questions.prompt: What is an asset tag used for?
questions.explanation: An asset tag helps IT identify and track equipment.

questions.prompt: A monitor says "No Signal." What is a good beginner-safe response if your department allows it?

options.label: Check power, cable connection, monitor input/source, and whether the computer is on

questions.explanation: Power, cable, input/source, and device power are safe first checks when approved by your department.

questions.prompt: A keyboard is not working. What should your summary include after an approved basic check?

options.label: The issue, what you checked, what happened, and whether more help is needed
A guess about who caused the problem

questions.explanation: Clear summaries help mentors and other IT staff understand the work.

questions.prompt: You are helping with imaging and do not know which image or workflow applies. What should you do?

options.label: Pick the image that sounds closest
Stop and ask your mentor or the IT tech on duty

questions.explanation: Using the wrong image can configure the computer incorrectly. Do not guess.

questions.prompt: An unfamiliar imaging error appears. What information should you collect before asking for help?
review_rubric: Includes device name, asset tag, or location when appropriate.
Captures the exact error message or code.
States that the student stopped and asked for help instead of guessing.
strong_answer_should_include: What the student was instructed to do
Whether the process stopped or continued
Confirmation that the student stopped and asked for help

questions.prompt: Draft a mentor summary for this situation: You checked a monitor issue at the front desk. The monitor had power, the DisplayPort cable was connected, and the monitor still showed "No Signal."
review_rubric: Explains the issue and location clearly.
Uses mentor-safe next-step language instead of claiming resolution too early.
questions.strong_answer_example: Checked monitor issue at front desk workstation. Monitor had power and DisplayPort cable was connected. Monitor still showed No Signal. Stopped and asked mentor for next approved step.

questions.prompt: Draft a mentor summary for this situation: You observed an imaging error on a computer at the workbench. The error code was 0x00000000. You were not sure what it meant.
review_rubric: Includes the exact imaging error code.
Says what the student did not know.
Shows that the student stopped and escalated before continuing.
questions.strong_answer_example: Observed imaging error on workbench computer. Error code shown: 0x00000000. I was not sure what it meant, so I stopped before continuing and notified my mentor for next steps.

questions.prompt: Which situation should usually be escalated?

options.label: A user says they cannot access a system they normally use
A monitor cable is visibly unplugged and you were told to reconnect it
You are reading a training module
You are checking your own schedule

questions.explanation: Access and permission issues should usually be escalated because they can affect security and user access.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you are unsure whether a task is beginner-safe?

options.label: Search randomly and follow the first result
Stop, document what you know, and ask your mentor
Tell the user IT cannot help

questions.explanation: Stopping and asking protects users, devices, data, and the team.
